title.narrative: DG ECHO PILOT PROGRAMMATIC PARTNERSHIP PROGRAMME (PPP), Accelerating local action in humanitarian and health crises in South Sudan

description.narrative: Risk Reduction activities will be undertaken in Eastern Equatoria and Northern Bahr el Ghazal while emergency response actions will have a countrywide coverage (supporting communities affected by disasters in any part of the country).

South Sudan is also severely affected by the outbreak of diseases including, Cholera, Malaria and the COVID-19 pandemic. Malaria and diarrhoeal diseases contribute significantly to the community disease burden and call for continued engagement and sensitization of communities to reduce the risk of exposure of these diseases. Combined with the low coverage in basic water and sanitation. low levels of development and high levels of poverty, the population remains vulnerable to the adverse effects of health shocks and stresses. This calls for a concerted effort to enhance the population's resilience and protect lives in disaster prone areas of the country.

This project aims to contribute to enhanced capacity of communities, SSRC and public authorities through mainstreaming Risk Communication Community Engagement (RCCE), including participatory VCA that informs the design of other activities, such as the development of contingency plans, awareness raising activities, training programmes, and the setting up of EWEA systems and two-way feedback communication mechanism.

This project aims to contribute to enhanced capacity of communities, SSRC and public authorities to address complex humanitarian and health crises in South Sudan through integrated interventions in three of the five PPP pillars: 1) Disaster Risk Management, 2) Epidemics/Pandemics and 3) Cash and Voucher Assistance.

he project aims at targeting 129.800 direct and indirect beneficiaries. A detailed description of target beneficiaries will be developed during the initial assessment planned at the start of this action. The community will lead targeting of community members to receive assistance through community-based targeting.
